purpose: S3 plan section 0 step 0: journeys for the owner-gated walked audit

horizon.basis: the gap below a horizon that visibly bound is weak evidence the horizon is right; the arrays can falsify a horizon claim and cannot verify one, and a sparse frontier leaves a real gap, so this is not provenance

min_possible_s.rule: seconds where OK, horizon_s where BEYOND_HORIZON, 0 where OFF_NETWORK
min_possible_s.soundness: 0 never exceeds the real bound, so the reconstruction can only report UNKNOWN where the pipeline proves FAIL; it can never manufacture an exclusion. It is NOT outcome-identical over the surface: OFF_NETWORK access is >= max_access_m, so the real bound is unbounded above

exact_for_emitted_rows.why: only OFF_NETWORK cells adjacent to an OK cell are emitted, and adjacency bounds their access by max_access_m + one cell diagonal

buildings.licence_use: count raster only; individual footprints are not read or republished

predicted_walk.note: the cap and this budget cover only rows with a finite predicted time; an OFF_NETWORK row has none, and adjacency to a PASS bounds its distance to the indexed network, not the length of the walk

blind_spot: The layer's aggregation is cost_selected_category: the time of the journey our cost model selected, an UPPER BOUND, not the minimum over qualifying destinations. The selected destination's identity is not stored either, so this audit establishes that some qualifying destination was open and reachable, never that ours was. Narrowing, not closing, the closed-destination blind spot that E1 and E2 share; closing it needs one bounded graph load over the sampled cells, keeping the POI-to-node association.

attribution.buildings_in_cell: Derived from Overture Maps buildings, release 2026-10-21.0, aggregated to counts per cell. No footprint geometry is reproduced. Upstream in this metro: OpenStreetMap (454,012 rows, ODbL 1.0), Microsoft ML Buildings (360,755 rows, ODbL 1.0 -- NOT CC BY, which an earlier version of this notice said) and Esri Community Maps contributors (26,653 rows, CC BY 4.0 with OpenStreetMap waivers). ODbL 4.3 and CC BY 3 notice obligations apply to a count raster as much as to geometry; see docs/experiments/audit/README.md and project-v2-rethink-decisions decision 17.
attribution.travel_times: our own routing over an OpenStreetMap extract (ODbL 1.0). Running our own router does not remove the source-database notice

seconds_precision: The stored seconds are float32. A model value of 600.00001 s is stored as 600.0 and so passes a 600 s threshold the model fails. This audit evaluates the stored artifact, which is what the product ships, not the model's float64 answer.
reproducibility: v2/data/ is gitignored, so the input rasters named above do not travel with a clone: this sheet is reproducible only on a machine that holds them. Rebuild with `uv run python spikes/s2_building_weighted_coverage.py grocery walk`, which needs data/triangle/roads.graphml (670 MB). The sha256s identify the inputs on a machine that has them.

superseded_by_rebuild.why: ab01ffa fixed `symmetrise` eight hours after the stored raster was built; `surface` and `vehicle` were also added to EXTRA_WAY_TAGS, which changes the profile digest and no walk-layer answer
superseded_by_rebuild.sample_not_redrawn_because: one journey has been walked against this draw; a redraw on the changed surface would select different cells and discard that observation
superseded_by_rebuild.digests_above_describe: v2/data/layers/prerebuild-2026-11-10/, where the arrays this sheet was drawn from are preserved
